issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Course instance method addRating(stars:) (external parameter label 'stars'), and the template provides a stub with that signature. However, the solution implementation defines addRating(rating:) (external label 'rating') while the solution's Client.swift still calls addRating(stars:). This creates an internal mismatch in the solution (Client calls a method label that does not exist) and a cross-artifact mismatch between the solution and the problem/template. Students following the problem and template would implement addRating(stars:), but the solution uses a different parameter label, and the solution as provided would not compile due to the inconsistent labels.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem and template by renaming the solution's Course.addRating parameter to use the external label 'stars' (func addRating(stars: Int)) and update any internal uses accordingly, or alternatively update the template/problem to require addRating(rating:) and change all calls (including Client.swift) to that label. Prefer preserving the problem/template signature (stars) to avoid confusing students.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template ask for an instance method addRating(stars:) on Course, but the solution implements the method as addRating(rating:). The parameter label differs (stars vs rating), which can confuse students mapping the requirement to the final implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the parameter label across all artifacts. Either change the solution method signature to func addRating(stars: Int) { ... } or update the problem statement and template to consistently use addRating(rating: Int). Prefer matching the problem/template (addRating(stars:)) to avoid confusing students.
